caption: The drawing depicts a single powder horn, prominently centered and slightly tilted to the right, with the base of the horn at the top left and the pointed end at the bottom right. The horn features a gradient of colors, including hues of yellow, green, brown, and a hint of purple, giving it a realistic appearance. The base is a circular, flat wooden plug—brown in color—secured with several nails or pins, and the plug displays visible cracks. Near the wider end of the horn, there are engravings that include the date "1865" and the initials "J.D." The tapering end of the horn is fitted with a short, darker brown spout for dispensing powder. The background consists of a light, off-white paper with a faint rectangular border sketched around the horn. In the bottom right corner, the artist's name, "Annie B. Johnston," is written in small, neat script.
title: Powder Horn
